title: "T-1 — the O5 gap decomposition: the ≤2x breach is protocol work volume (10.96x), not kernel time"
---

Date: 2026-11-28. Task: review-06 §9 T-1 (P1, "read-only on the m7
ledger; the number that directs everything"). Method: a census over the
committed floor table (`bench/m7/tools/matrix_governance.py`
`_FLOOR_ANCHORS`, 189 anchors = 9 tools × 21 classes, all reps=100,
cpu-basis metric of record) plus the runners that define what each side
EXECUTES per cell. Every figure below re-reads committed bytes; nothing
is asserted from lore. No measurement was re-run: this decomposition is
arithmetic over the sealed ledger.

## 1. What each side of the parity row actually executes (the decisive inputs)

**(a) The faces run a 4000-fit documented-defaults extraction chain on a
single-sample catalog.** The m7 cell runner drives
`bp_extract_signatures(catalog, seed = seed)` at documented defaults
(zero-override law, `bench/m7/adapters/run_sigminer_arm.R:16-24`); the
witnessed sigminer signature is
`bp_extract_signatures(nmf_matrix, range = 2:5, n_bootstrap = 20L,
n_nmf_run = 50, ...)` — **4 ranks × 20 bootstraps × 50 runs = 4000 NMF
fits per rep**, exactly the "frozen 20x50x4 geometry / the 4000
certified fits" the batch face records
(`bench/m7/competitors/p6_arms.py:111-116`), plus the smaller K-survey CV
leg. The input per rep is **one 96-channel counts vector**
(`bench/g0/g0/sim.py::sample_cell` — one multinomial/NB draw per
(arm, n, rep)): the N axis (100 → 1,000,000) scales mutation MASS, never
matrix geometry. Every O5 cell is a 96×1 extraction.

**(b) The yardstick runs one NNLS assignment solve.** The sigprofiler
yardstick is SigProfilerAssignment v1.1.5
`Analyzer.cosmic_fit` at documented defaults
(`bench/m7/adapters/run_sigprofiler.py` header): a catalog-assignment
NNLS over a fixed 96×101 system — a fundamentally lighter workload than
a de novo extraction chain, by each tool's own documented best practice.

## 3. The decomposition — an exact log-additive identity, not a model

Over the 21 classes, per-rep cpu factors (geomeans):

| factor | evidence | value |
|--------|----------|------:|
| **K** — R interpreter → certified kernel (same protocol, spawn) | `post_v3` vs `post_v3_rust` twins | **2.602x bought** |
| **T** — spawn-per-fit transport → batch bridge | `post_v3_rust` vs `post_v3_rust_batch` | **1.435x bought** |
| **W** — protocol work volume (batch face vs yardstick) | `post_v3_rust_batch` / `sigprofiler` | **10.96x REMAINING** |

Identity check (log-additive): `breach_R ÷ K ÷ T = W` — at the ledger's
full precision 40.9041 / 2.6016 / 1.4347 = 10.9589, where the identity
holds **by construction**, not by fit: K and T are ratios of the same
committed cells that compose breach_R, and W is the batch face over the
same yard cells. At the 4-significant-figure roundings quoted in the
table the chain reproduces W to ~0.04% (40.904 / 2.602 / 1.435 =
10.955 vs 10.959).

**Kernel time (the review's factor 1) is bounded out of the remaining
gap.** The measured kernel-side levers are: faer 0.24.4 through the same
four-pass KL structure at 1.31x (96×1000) / 1.20x (96×4000) — and the O5
cells are 96×1, *skinnier than every probed shape*, where per-call
overhead already dominates arithmetic (per-fit all-in cost on the batch
face ≈ 4.0 s ÷ 4000 ≈ **1.0 ms/fit**; the spawn face adds ≈ 0.44 ms/fit
of transport). Even the full faer 1.31x applied to W leaves
10.96/1.31 = 8.37x — still **4.18x above the ≤2x bar** (5.48x before
any kernel gain) — that no kernel-time lever can supply. The bit-identity wall is not the binding
constraint; arithmetic itself forbids the kernel route to parity.

**Shape mix (the review's factor 3) measures ≈ absent.** The yardstick
is flat in N across the entire class axis: 0.346-0.423 s/rep (×1.22
spread) from N=100 to N=1,000,000 — because NNLS assignment on a fixed
96×101 system does not see mutation mass. The faces are equally flat
(batch 3.880-4.968 s/rep, ×1.28). The single class where mass visibly
moves cost is comp_pole@1M (W=14.26x, +30% over the W geomean); the
pole family (anchored only at N ∈ {10⁵, 3×10⁵, 10⁶}) also shows the R
face getting *cheaper* with N (11.06 → 9.54 → 8.54 s/rep) while the
kernel faces get slightly costlier (5.92 → 6.08 → 6.80 s/rep spawn;
4.11 → 4.31 → 4.97 s/rep batch) — an R-side iteration-count quirk of
saturated spectra, noted for completeness, not load-bearing.

**Work volume (the review's factor 2) owns the breach.** 4000+
documented-default NMF fits per rep versus one NNLS solve per rep:
10.96x at geomean, 9.44-14.26x per class. It is *protocol-inherited*
(sigminer's documented best practice, zero-override law) — no engine
work can touch it.

## 4. Consequences (what this number directs)

1. **The ≤2x sigprofiler parity row is unreachable by engine
   optimization.** K and T are already banked (2.602x × 1.435x); the
   kernel-time ceiling is measured at ≤1.31x and the shape axis is
   empty. Closing the row means moving W, and W is made of protocol
   work: 4000 fits per rep.
2. **T-3 (work-volume lane) is thereby scoped to the protocol, not the
   kernel**, and every candidate lever lives on one of three shelves:
   (i) *inside-fit* budgets (early stopping / convergence tolerance —
   RTOL=1e-3 is bp's own default) — these change produced digits, so
   they need the re-anchoring ruling that is already declined by user
   order (2026-11-27) for the anchors' lifetime; (ii) *initialization
   quality* (NNDSVDa vs random) — fewer wasted restarts, bit-identity
   breaking at the seed law, same re-anchoring class; (iii) *protocol
   volume* (n_bootstrap/n_nmf_run/range) — these are sigminer's
   documented defaults; touching them abandons the zero-override law
   and requires a NEW pre-registered arm, never a silent widening of
   the existing 147/168 rows.
3. **The parity row's semantics deserve a user-owned re-scope decision**
   (surface-only, like the L6 ruling): the row compares a de novo
   extraction chain against a catalog assignment solve because those
   are the tools' documented best practices for the same deliverable
   (per-sample exposures on the same truth). The accuracy program is
   untouched; the ≤2x TIME bar against an assignment yardstick is the
   definition that T-1 now shows cannot be met by engine work. Options
   for the user: re-scope the yardstick (a de novo SigProfilerExtractor
   leg), re-base the bar on W-adjusted parity (equal-work comparison),
   or retire the row to an honest statement of protocol cost.
4. **The paper's performance chapter (T-9) now has its honest
   spine**: the breach decomposes exactly into banked engineering
   (2.60x × 1.43x) and protocol volume (10.96x); the kernel program's
   measured ceiling (L1-L5 1.223x step-core, faer ≤1.31x) is a
   rounding error against W.
